text: The first sign was the coffee. Mara Okafor poured it at 6:42 a.m., as she did every weekday. She watched the dark ribbon leave the pot and fill her chipped blue mug. Then she watched it rise back out, every drop climbing obediently home, until the mug was empty and dry and the clock on the stove read 6:41. She blinked. The pot was full. Outside, a sparrow that had just landed on the windowsill lifted off backward, tail-first, into a sky that was a shade less pink than it had been a moment ago. Mara set the pot down very carefully, because her hands had started to shake, and because some small, cold part of her already understood that she had done this. She hadn't simply witnessed it. The world hadn't slipped. *She* had pulled it, the way you might tug a loose thread on a sweater. Somewhere beneath her ribs she could still feel the thread, taut and humming, waiting to see how hard she would pull next.
